text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Galaxy Media has sent to Communications Minister Richard Alston top legal advice from David Catterns QC that its R-rated Nightmoves pay-TV service, which operates between 11pm and 4am for an additional fee and only with a PIN number, is within both the "letter" and the "spirit" of the Broadcasting Services Act, which regulates pay-TV. Page 3. --

The Australian Securities Commission has laid charges on Brian Conway, the founding chairman of Cambridge Gulf Exploration NL, and Malcolm McLeod, a former geologist and consultant to the company, over circumstances leading to the release of a report on Cambridge's diamond exploration program in December 1993. Page 4.

According to the latest survey of companies prepared by the National Australia Bank NAB.AX, the economy is set for a strong recovery over the coming year, with economic growth tipped to be above four per cent by the end of 1997, despite current conditions, which are still subdued and vary considerably across industries. Page 5.

Two recent court decisions in the United States appear to have reduced the chances of a massive damages award against Pacific Dunlop Ltd for the failure of its Telectronics heart pacemaker leads. PacDun have argued that while all cases against the company concern the use of Telectronics' Accufix J atrial pacemaker leads, each case is unique, and so unable to be argued under a class action. Page 17.

It has been revealed that the senior executives and staff of Colonial Mutual may enjoy up to a 4.6 per cent share of the bancassurance group after its listing on the Australian Stock Exchange, and that chief executive Peter Smedley committed to a five year contract with Colonial Mutual last December that would entitle him to remuneration of A$988,000 per annum. Page 17.

Both Australian Retail Investments, and interests associated with the company, have questioned the shareholders of Country Road over Country Road's CTY.AX 50 per cent drop in interim profit to A$1.08 million. ARI, which owns over nine per cent of Country Road, is focused on the intentions of certain institutional investors on the Country Road share register. Page 17.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Commenting on the Bank of Melbourne's increase in fees - just 24 hours after a A$1 billion takeover offer by Westpac Banking Corp, industry regulator Professor Allan Fels, speaking on the Nine Network's Business Sunday program yesterday, said bank fees will be examined as part of any assessment of the merger. Page 17.

In a wide-ranging interview on the Business Sunday program yesterday, Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Allan Fels indicated telecommunications companies faced fines of more than A$10 million for anti-competitive behaviour when the sector is deregulated from July 1 and the ACCC takes over as principal watchdog. Page 17.

The once-promising marriage between Pacific Dunlop Ltd and French group Fleury Michon - the two announced a joint venture initiative in a food processing deal with a A$15 million high-tech manufacturing facility in Echuca, Victoria - is now headed for an acrimonious arbitration hearing, which under the terms of the joint-venture agreement will take place in Paris later this year. Page 17.

According to Australian Broadcasting Authority documents, Canadian broadcasting group, CanWest Global Communications Corp, CGSs.TO financed the acquisition of shares in the Ten Group Ltd at a price it believed was "commercially outrageous". The comments were revealed after the ABA ruled on Friday that CanWest was in a position to acquire 52.49 per cent of the voting shares in Ten. Page 17.

According to the latest figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics, the three-year boom in minerals and petroleum exploration has continued, with spending on exploration for minerals other than petroleum increasing by a seasonally adjusted 8 per cent during the three months to December last year. Page 19.

In comments which substantiate the Federal Government's move to target Asia's A$70 billion food import market with its Supermarket to Asia plan, Mark Schmitt, whose family runs a potato farm on the banks of the Macquarie River, says he will probably double the farm's current output of 2,500 tonnes as exports to Korea and Singapore continue to grow. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Leading stockbrokers are to meet this week to discuss the creation of a secret lobby group to resent their views on how the Australian Stock Exchange should be run after its planned demutualisation. The ASX won approval last October from its stockbroker members to proceed with a change in its ownership from a mutual to a company. Page 33.

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Allan Fels indicated there would be major changes when the telecommunications sector is deregulated from July 1, saying players who breach the strict new competition rules face fines of up to A$10 million and possible legal action. Page 33.

In a result which Citibank chief economist Stephen Koukoulas says indicates overseas buyers have "put their money where their mouth is", foreign investment in Australian bonds is at record levels, with A$191.1 billion worth of Government bonds controlled by international investors. Page 33.

Following the Australian Securities Commission's court action earlier this year against Nomura International alleging market manipulation and misleading and deceptive conduct, Britain's Daily Telegraph reported on Saturday that the country's Securities and Futures Authority is investigating Nomura and two employees over its controversial A$600 million stockmarket play last March. Page 33.

Brian Conway, the former chief of Cambridge Gulf Exploration, who was last Friday committed for trial in the Perth District Court on two counts of misleading statements in breach of the Corporations Law, will know by Wednesday of Judge Christopher Carr's decision on the A$6 million summary judgement application lodged by CLC Corp against Conway and his family company, Penale Pty Ltd, over an alleged 1994 deal. Page 35.

In a unanimous decision yesterday, the Appeal Court dismissed an appeal from the Colonial State Bank against a 1994 Supreme Court ruling that Mr and Mrs V. Burke, an elderly couple who used their home to secure their son's A$40,000 loan extension, were not liable to pay that amount because Colonial failed to tell them their rights, electing instead to leave it to the couple's son to tell his parents the details. Page 35.
THE AGE

Patrick Stevedoring chairman Chris Corrigan said yesterday it will take legal action against the Melbourne Port Corporation's plan to bring in another cargo handler. Corrigan said the company would seek damages against the Corporation and the Victorian Government for breaching a deal which restricted competition at the port. Page B1.

The National Australia Bank March quarterly survey says business conditions are still sluggish, suffering from concerns in the manufacturing and retail industries, but enjoying good performances from the mining and financial sectors. The survey found slightly improved profitability, lower employment, and subdued business conditions. Page B1.

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Professor Allan Fels said on Channel Nine's Business Sunday yesterday that Westpac Banking Corporation would need to prove there would be no reduction in competition if it were to win approval from the ACCC for its proposed takeover of the Bank of Melbourne. Page B1.

Australia's leading stockbrokers will meet this week to discuss the future of the Australian Stock Exchange, after the ASX won approval to proceed with its demutualisation in October. Stockbrokers hope to form a secret lobby group to ensure they have a single voice to air their concerns over the planned set-up. Page B2.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has convinced the 18-member APEC group meeting in Cebu, Philippines, to support plans to crack down on "cyberspace" tax evaders. The APEC finance ministers agreed to review the impact of computer technologies and the Internet on tax revenues in coordination with the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development and the Asian Development Bank. Page B2.

The Securities and Futures Authority in Britain is investigating the activities of Robert Mapstone, the former head of equities of Nomura International, and Duncan Moss, a Hong Kong-based trader for the organisation, after allegations the men manipulated he Australian sharemarket last year, when Nomura International allowed 12,844 futures contracts on the Australian Stock Exchange to expire. This lead to the sale of shares worth A$600 million, and a 25-point fall on the Australian All Ordinaries. Page B3
